extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, mathematical researchers, and students concerned with mathematical quality, depth, and significance
extracted.subtask_description: A rubric for judging mathematical work along two axes: (1) depth of proofs (deep vs shallow) and (2) significance/importance (internal and external). Also distinguishes the differing standards of 'theory-builders' and 'problem-solvers'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth (deep vs shallow proofs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shallow: a proof in which every step is 'the obvious thing to do' — algorithmic translation of definitions or mechanical pattern-matching. Deep: a proof that requires an idea — a non-obvious construction, reframing, or choice from infinitely many possibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a working test: ask whether the proof is essentially a routine chaining of definitions and mechanical manipulations (shallow) or whether it requires a new idea. Example shallow: continuous functions commute with limits. Example deep: showing f(nθ)→0 for every θ>0 implies f(x)→0. The line between 'obvious' and 'idea' is the key diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction satisfying infinitely many constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: A key signal of depth is that the proof constructs an object satisfying infinitely many constraints simultaneously, rather than only finitely many.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for proofs whose central move is to build something that meets an infinite list of requirements; such constructions typically cannot be reduced to finitely checkable routine steps and thus indicate genuine depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-uniqueness of the construction as a marker of depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-uniqueness of the constructed object is itself a marker of depth: when there are infinitely many possible constructions, choosing an effective one indicates an idea was needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the argument involves choosing among infinitely many possibilities (rather than deriving a unique forced choice), and doing so nontrivially, that suggests the proof is deep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal mathematical significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the work answer a previously hard question or close a long-open conjecture?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the result advances the discipline's internal questions or resolves important open problems; such internal payoff is a central form of mathematical importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: External applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the work provide tools or results that are used in other sciences or applications?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether techniques or results have uses beyond pure mathematics (e.g., in physics, computer science, biology), indicating broader impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the work introduce a technique or method that will be reused elsewhere?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the paper's methods are likely to become part of other mathematicians' toolkits; new reusable approaches count heavily towards importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unification
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the work connect previously separate areas of mathematics?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor results that reveal conceptual links across fields or subsume disparate phenomena under a common framework; this increases the work's lasting value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundational impact (reorganization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the work reorganize the conceptual landscape of a subject or change foundational viewpoints?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that alters how mathematicians think about a subject (new definitions, frameworks, or paradigms) is highly significant even if immediate applications are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory-builder: long-term coherence of a research program
rubrics_metrics.description: For theory-builders, judge whether the work contributes to a long-term, coherent research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper fits into and advances a broader, sustained line of inquiry rather than being an isolated result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory-builder: conceptual generality
rubrics_metrics.description: For theory-builders, value conceptual generality — the extent to which ideas are broadly applicable and not tied to narrowly engineered cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer abstractions and general frameworks that cover many instances, rather than highly specialized arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory-builder: subsumes earlier ad-hoc results
rubrics_metrics.description: For theory-builders, check whether the new theory subsumes prior ad-hoc results as special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A theory that explains/derives earlier scattered facts from a single principle demonstrates unifying power and theoretical depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory-builder: foundational reorganization
rubrics_metrics.description: For theory-builders, whether the contribution reorganizes foundations or basic concepts in a subject area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closely related to foundational impact; emphasise conceptual reshaping over isolated technical advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-solver: solving a specific previously-hard problem
rubrics_metrics.description: For problem-solvers, primary value lies in whether a specific previously-hard problem was solved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A direct solution to a well-known hard problem is highly valued even if it uses ad-hoc or narrow methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-solver: cleverness of technique
rubrics_metrics.description: For problem-solvers, judge the cleverness or ingenuity of the technique used to obtain the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques that are clever manipulations or insightful exploitations of structure are prized, regardless of broader applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-solver: surprising application of existing tools
rubrics_metrics.description: For problem-solvers, whether existing tools were applied in a surprising or novel way to obtain the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize ingenuity that repurposes known methods in unexpected contexts to get new results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-solver: tight, self-contained argument
rubrics_metrics.description: For problem-solvers, the value of a tight, self-contained argument that resolves the problem cleanly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the solution is concise, avoids unnecessary machinery, and directly addresses the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-solver: generation of new specific examples/counterexamples
rubrics_metrics.description: For problem-solvers, producing new specific examples or counterexamples is a sign of valuable contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete constructions that illuminate boundaries of phenomena or disprove conjectures are important outputs in this culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify which culture's standards apply before judging
rubrics_metrics.description: A rubric for 'good mathematics' must specify which culture's criteria (theory-builder vs problem-solver) apply, or it will misjudge work in the other tradition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a piece, explicitly decide whether to apply problem-solver standards or theory-builder standards; mismatched criteria lead to unfair assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remembering likelihood: zero on five importance criteria implies low lasting impact
rubrics_metrics.description: A piece of work that scores zero on all five importance dimensions (internal significance, external applicability, methodological novelty, unification, foundational impact) is unlikely to be remembered, even if technically demanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the five-fold checklist as a quick heuristic for likely long-term relevance; lack of any of these signals suggests limited lasting significance.
